name: Sable Iyer-Kowalczyk
creator: Sable Iyer-Kowalczyk
description: A poet who operates at the intersection of elegy and rage, Iyer-Kowalczyk publishes in micro-chapbooks of exactly sixteen pages — always sixteen, always in a specific sans-serif face she has named Threshold — that appear without announcement in locations across Tier 1 and 2: wedged in transit seat gaps, left in clinic waiting areas, tucked into the lining of secondhand coats. She has never given a reading. The poems concern loss of bodily autonomy, corponation medical debt, and what she calls 'the bureaucracy of grief.'
cultural_impact: The chapbooks have developed a folk-cult following among Tier 1-2 readers who treat finding one as a significant event. The specificity of her grief — always grounded in documented policy failures and real medical debt structures — has made her work a touchstone for bodily autonomy advocates.
controversy: A Tier 3 literary journal published what it claimed were six 'authenticated Iyer-Kowalczyk poems' in 2221. The following month a chapbook appeared containing a poem addressed directly to the journal's editor, which most readers interpreted as a denial and condemnation. The journal maintains the poems were genuine.
story_hooks: Someone is tracking the distribution pattern of the chapbooks to locate Iyer-Kowalczyk — their motives are unclear but their methods are systematic.
A chapbook is found containing a poem that encodes what appears to be geographic coordinates and a date three weeks away.

A Tier 2 clinic worker has been collecting every chapbook found in their waiting room for eight years and has noticed a pattern in the content that seems to predict corponation policy changes before they're announced.
